senses.definition: The watery liquid your mouth makes to moisten food and start breaking it down.
senses.example: Saliva helps make a dry cracker easier to swallow.

senses.definition: A small part or measurement taken from something larger.
senses.example: A microphone recording can hold many sound samples from each second.

senses.definition: Water with dissolved materials that moves through plants, including the sugar-rich liquid collected from some maple trees.
senses.example: Maple sap dripped into the line leading from the tree.

senses.definition: Describes a mixture that already holds as much of a dissolved substance as it can under its current conditions.
senses.example: More salt stayed on the bottom after the water was saturated with salt.

senses.definition: One of a group of dinosaurs with long necks and tails that walked on four legs and ate plants.
senses.example: Brachiosaurus was a sauropod with especially long front legs.

senses.definition: An open area of grass with scattered trees, often in a warm place with a wet season and a dry season.
senses.example: Zebras grazed on the savanna while birds rested in a tree.

senses.definition: To speak words or show a message in writing.
senses.example: Mari said we should wait until the light turned green.

senses.definition: A chance to give your opinion or help make a decision.
senses.example: Each team member had a say in choosing the name.

senses.definition: A tool that shows how heavy something is.
senses.example: I put the apples on the kitchen scale.

senses.definition: The way a distance in a map or a size in a model compares to the real distance or size.
senses.example: The map’s scale shows that one inch on the page stands for ten miles.

senses.definition: One of the small, thin pieces on the outside of many fish and reptiles.
senses.example: Each scale on the fish caught a bit of light.

senses.definition: A set of musical notes played in order from low to high or high to low.
senses.example: I practiced a scale on the piano before playing my song.

senses.definition: To climb up or over something tall or difficult.
senses.example: The climbers wore safety gear to scale the wall.

senses.definition: Singing made-up sounds or syllables in place of words, often in jazz.
senses.example: The quick scat singing sounded almost like a trumpet solo.

senses.definition: Software that can turn computer text and controls into spoken words or braille.
senses.example: The screen reader spoke the name of the button.

senses.definition: The written words and directions for a play, movie, or other performance.
senses.example: The script told the actor when to cross the stage.

senses.definition: Art that takes up space in three directions or rises out from a surface.
senses.example: We walked around the sculpture to look at it from behind.

senses.definition: The salt water that covers much of Earth, or one particular part of that water.
senses.example: From the hill we could see the sea and the boats far away.

senses.definition: A flowering plant that grows under the sea with roots and long leaves.
senses.example: The green turtle bit off a piece of seagrass in shallow water.

senses.definition: A program or service that looks through a list of information to find matches for your question.
senses.example: I asked a search engine for pages about parrots.

senses.definition: Small pieces of sand, clay or other material that settle after moving through water or air.
senses.example: A layer of sediment gathered at the bottom of the pond.

senses.definition: Rock made from settled grains or from other material that collects in a layer and hardens.
senses.example: Grains of sand held together can form a sedimentary rock called sandstone.

senses.definition: To notice something with your eyes.
senses.example: We saw three birds sitting on a wire.

senses.definition: To understand what someone means or how something works.
senses.example: I see why both pieces need to be the same length now.

senses.definition: A plant part that holds a tiny young plant and can grow into a new plant in the right conditions.
senses.example: We planted a bean seed in a cup of soil.

senses.definition: To put seeds in or on the ground so plants can grow.
senses.example: We will seed the bare patch of lawn in spring.

senses.definition: A place or collection that stores seeds to preserve different plants for the future.
senses.example: The seed bank stored seeds from many kinds of rice.

senses.definition: The store of seeds already in the soil in a place.
senses.example: After rain, some seeds in the soil’s seed bank began to grow.

senses.definition: Forced separation of groups of people, such as rules that keep children of different races in separate schools.
senses.example: Families went to court to challenge segregation in public schools.

senses.definition: To cause a thing, message, or person to go to another place.
senses.example: We sent a postcard to our cousins.

senses.definition: A device that notices or measures something, such as warmth, pressure, or motion.
senses.example: The sensor told the robot that it had bumped the wall.

senses.definition: An electric circuit with its parts arranged along one path for current.
senses.example: The lamps in a series circuit both go out if one place in the path breaks.

senses.definition: The stated amount of food or drink used to work out the numbers on a food label.
senses.example: The serving size printed on the label is half a cup.

senses.definition: The time and place where a story happens.
senses.example: The setting of the story was a snowy town many years ago.

senses.definition: Marks or color that show the lighter and darker parts of a drawing.
senses.example: A little shading helped the drawn ball look round.

senses.definition: An animal related to a goat, often raised for its wool, milk, or meat.
senses.example: The farmer counted six sheep in the field.

senses.definition: To give off light or look bright as light bounces off something.
senses.example: The full moon shone above the rooftops.

senses.definition: To make something look bright by cleaning or polishing it.
senses.example: I shined my shoes for the concert.

senses.definition: To let someone see something, or help them see how to do it.
senses.example: I showed my friend how to fold a paper boat.

senses.definition: A performance or program for people to see or hear.
senses.example: The school put on a puppet show.

senses.definition: The light object hit over a net in badminton, shaped with a rounded base and a wide skirt.
senses.example: The shuttlecock slowed and dropped near the net.

senses.definition: A sign or message that tells what is happening or what to do.
senses.example: The bell was our signal to go inside.

senses.definition: To send someone a sign or message.
senses.example: We waved to signal that we were ready.

senses.definition: A comparison that uses a word like “as” or “like” to connect different things.
senses.example: “As quiet as falling snow” is a simile.

senses.definition: To make music with your voice by moving among notes.
senses.example: We sang a song on the bus.

senses.definition: To rest your body on your bottom with the upper part of your body usually upright.
senses.example: We sat on a bench to rest our feet.

senses.definition: A muscle that can help move your body by pulling on a bone.
senses.example: A skeletal muscle in your upper arm helps bend your elbow.

senses.definition: The hard frame of bones that supports a person or animal.
senses.example: An X-ray can show part of your skeleton.

senses.definition: The thin, living cover on the outside of the body.
senses.example: Skin lets me feel the bumps on this leaf.

senses.definition: The group of bones that shapes the head and surrounds the brain.
senses.example: The skull protects the brain.

senses.definition: To be in the natural resting state in which you are less aware of things around you and may dream.
senses.example: I slept until the birds started to sing.

senses.definition: The natural period of rest when a person or animal is asleep.
senses.example: A night of good sleep helped me feel ready for school.

senses.definition: The programs and other instructions a computer uses to do its work.
senses.example: Drawing software can turn my finger movements into a colored line.

senses.definition: The Sun and the objects held near it by gravity, including planets, moons, comets, and asteroids. Systems around other stars are often called planetary systems.
senses.example: Earth is one of eight planets in our solar system.

senses.definition: A flow of tiny charged particles that keeps blowing outward from the Sun.
senses.example: The solar wind carries pieces of the Sun’s outer atmosphere out into space.

senses.definition: A kind of matter that keeps its own shape under ordinary conditions.
senses.example: Ice is a solid, but it can melt into liquid water.

senses.definition: Made of material all the way through, with no empty middle.
senses.example: The toy was carved from one solid piece of wood.

senses.definition: Firm or strong enough to stay steady.
senses.example: The table needed a solid base so it would not wobble.

senses.definition: Either of the two moments each year when a hemisphere tilts farthest toward or away from the Sun.
senses.example: Near the June solstice, summer days are longest in places north of the equator.

senses.definition: The amount of one substance that can dissolve in a certain amount of another under given conditions.
senses.example: Heat can change the solubility of sugar in water.

senses.definition: An even mixture formed when one substance dissolves in another.
senses.example: Stirring salt into water made a salt solution.

senses.definition: A way to find objects or measure distance using sound, often under water.
senses.example: The crew used sonar to make a map of the seafloor.

senses.definition: Putting things into a useful order or groups, such as from smallest to largest.
senses.example: Sorting the cards made it easier to find the number I wanted.

senses.definition: Vibrations that travel through material such as air, water, or a wall and can often be heard.
senses.example: The sound of the bell reached us from across the playground.

senses.definition: To make a noise or to seem a certain way to someone who hears you.
senses.example: You sound excited about your trip.

senses.definition: In good condition or based on good reasons.
senses.example: The builder checked that the old steps were sound.

senses.definition: To use your voice to say words. It can also mean being able to use a language.
senses.example: She spoke slowly so the whole class could follow.

senses.definition: A group of living things of the same kind. Members of many species can have young with one another, though scientists also use other clues to tell species apart.
senses.example: The blue whale and the humpback whale are different species.

senses.definition: A round three-dimensional shape with every point on its surface the same distance from its center.
senses.example: The ball was almost a perfect sphere.

senses.definition: A thick bundle of nerve tissue protected by the backbone that carries many messages between the brain and body.
senses.example: Signals that help move your foot can travel through your spinal cord.

senses.definition: A tiny cell that can grow into a new living thing in suitable conditions.
senses.example: A fern released spores from spots under its leaves.

senses.definition: A computer table where you can organize values and use calculations based on them.
senses.example: My spreadsheet added all the numbers in the last column.

senses.definition: A wheel with teeth that fit into openings in a chain.
senses.example: The pedals turn a sprocket that pulls the bicycle chain.

senses.definition: A mineral formation that grows downward from the roof of a cave as water leaves material behind.
senses.example: A drop hung for a moment at the tip of a stalactite.

senses.definition: A mineral formation that grows upward from a cave floor as water drops leave material behind.
senses.example: The rounded stalagmite grew where drops hit the same spot.

senses.definition: To stay upright on your feet.
senses.example: We stood at the fence to watch the parade.

senses.definition: A frame or base that holds an object up.
senses.example: The music stand held the pages at the right height.

senses.definition: A small place where people sell or hand out things.
senses.example: A roadside stand sold baskets of berries.

senses.definition: A group of lines in a poem, often separated from other lines by an empty space.
senses.example: The poem had two stanzas of four lines each.

senses.definition: A huge ball of hot gas in space that gives off its own light. The Sun is the nearest one to Earth.
senses.example: A star can look like a tiny point because it is so far away.

senses.definition: A shape with points sticking out from the center.
senses.example: We drew a five-pointed star on the card.

senses.definition: A person who is especially well known for performing or doing something.
senses.example: She became a basketball star.

senses.definition: To play one of the main parts in a show, film, or play.
senses.example: I hope to star in the school play someday.

senses.definition: A long chain of sugar units found in foods such as rice, flour, or potatoes.
senses.example: Starch in the potato can be broken into smaller sugars.

senses.definition: The main physical forms matter can take, including solid, liquid and gas.
senses.example: Ice, liquid water and water vapor are three states of matter.

senses.definition: Electric charge that has collected somewhere rather than flowing steadily through a path.
senses.example: Static electricity made the balloon pull toward the wall.

senses.definition: An upright carved slab or pillar, often put up to remember a person or event.
senses.example: The carved stele stood near an old grave.

senses.definition: The part of a plant that holds up leaves, flowers, or other parts and carries materials between them.
senses.example: A sunflower has a tall stem.

senses.definition: A picture or artwork showing objects such as fruit, cups, flowers, or books.
senses.example: Our still life showed three apples and a glass bowl.

senses.definition: A tiny opening in a plant surface. Water vapor and gases move through it.
senses.example: A microscope showed each stoma on the underside of the leaf.

senses.definition: The part of your body that holds food after you swallow it and mixes it with juices.
senses.example: Food moves from the stomach into the small intestine.

senses.definition: A part or place that keeps information for the computer to use later.
senses.example: The picture was saved in storage and still appeared after I restarted.

senses.definition: A narrow stretch of water that connects two larger bodies of water.
senses.example: The ship crossed the strait between the two islands.

senses.definition: A repeated movement or set of movements used in an activity such as swimming or rowing.
senses.example: The swimmer practiced the breaststroke kick as part of a new stroke.

senses.definition: Strong and able to stand up to weight, use, or bumps.
senses.example: We packed the books in a sturdy box.

senses.definition: A word part added at the end of a word or word part. It can change the meaning or how a word works in a sentence.
senses.example: Adding the suffix -less to care makes careless.

senses.definition: The right to vote in an election.
senses.example: Supporters of women’s suffrage worked for women to be able to vote.

senses.definition: A huge explosion of a star or of certain remains of a star.
senses.example: The supernova grew bright enough for astronomers to see from very far away.

senses.definition: A pulling effect at the surface of a liquid that makes its surface tend to shrink.
senses.example: Surface tension helped pull a drop of rain into a rounded shape.

senses.definition: To move through water by moving your body, legs, fins, or arms.
senses.example: The ducks swam across the pond in a line.

senses.definition: A group of written signs. Each sign generally stands for one spoken syllable rather than a single sound.
senses.example: Sequoyah made a syllabary for writing Cherokee.

senses.definition: One beat or part of a spoken word, usually built around a vowel sound.
senses.example: Clap once for each syllable in butterfly: but-ter-fly.

senses.definition: A balance that lets one part of a shape match another part when you fold, turn, or move it in a certain way.
senses.example: The two sides of a paper heart can show symmetry.

senses.definition: Spinning once for every trip around a neighboring body, so one side stays facing that body.
senses.example: The Moon’s synchronous rotation keeps nearly the same side facing Earth.
